# CSIP Test Device PKI (self-minted, §6.11-compliant)

Self-minted test material generated by the `sep2server certs` tooling built
from `cmd/sep2server`. Not from any real device or vendor. Reproducible from
the commands below.

## Files

| File               | Contents                                                              |
|--------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `root_ca.pem`      | Self-signed ECDSA P-256 root CA.                                      |
| `device_chain.pem` | Device leaf cert followed by the root CA, concatenated PEM.           |
| `device_key.pem`   | Device leaf private key (ECDSA P-256, unencrypted PKCS#8).           |

## Device identity

| Field | Value                                      |
|-------|--------------------------------------------|
| SFDI  | `397028461857` (display `397-028-461-857`) |
| LFDI  | `93E795AE91F5F493813E3B39C8BC49F06FCA6258` |

LFDI is the first 20 bytes of `SHA-256(leaf.DER)`, hex-uppercase. SFDI is
the top 36 bits of the same hash, formatted as 11 zero-padded decimal digits
plus a sum-of-digits mod-10 check digit.

## Cert attributes

The device leaf is CSIP §6.11-compliant:

- Key: ECDSA P-256
- Signature algorithm: `ecdsa-with-SHA256`
- Subject: empty (per spec)
- SAN (critical): HardwareModuleName OtherName, hwType OID `1.3.6.1.4.1.40732`,
  hwSerialNum `CSIPTEST-DEVICE-001`
- KeyUsage: DigitalSignature + KeyAgreement
- ExtKeyUsage: ClientAuth
- CertificatePolicies (critical): `1.3.6.1.4.1.40732.1.1` (generic device)
  and `1.3.6.1.4.1.40732.2.1` (device-auth-test)

The CA cert is also ECDSA P-256 with maxValidity (valid through 9999-12-31).

## How to regenerate

Build and run the server binary from the repo root:

```sh
go build -o /tmp/sep2server ./cmd/sep2server

/tmp/sep2server certs generate-ca \
  --cn "CSIP Test Device CA" --org "" --years 0 \
  --out /tmp/testdevice-pki

/tmp/sep2server certs generate-device \
  --ca /tmp/testdevice-pki/ca.crt \
  --ca-key /tmp/testdevice-pki/ca.key \
  --hw-serial "CSIPTEST-DEVICE-001" \
  --hw-type "1.3.6.1.4.1.40732" \
  --name device --test \
  --out /tmp/testdevice-pki

# Build the chain (leaf first, then CA)
cat /tmp/testdevice-pki/device.crt /tmp/testdevice-pki/ca.crt \
  > testdata/csip-pki/testdevice/device_chain.pem
cp /tmp/testdevice-pki/device.key \
   testdata/csip-pki/testdevice/device_key.pem
cp /tmp/testdevice-pki/ca.crt \
   testdata/csip-pki/testdevice/root_ca.pem
```

Each regeneration produces different keys (and therefore different SFDI/LFDI
values) because the private key is freshly sampled. Update the identity table
above and any fixture YAML that hardcodes the SFDI/LFDI if you regenerate.
